name: define two letters by how a word happens to be spelled
one_line: A clue whose answer is two letters, and which points not at what a word means but at how it happens to be written.
how: Print three worked clues with their answers — «La fine del giorno» is NO, «In mezzo all'Arno» is RN, «I confini del Venezuela» is VA — and then the one thing that makes them work: the meaning of the named word does not matter, only its spelling. Name the four moves, which are the start, the end, the middle and the two ends together. Then print four answers with blank lines above them and ask for the clues: LA, RA, RE, ES. The middle of MILANO gives LA, the ends of ROMA give RA, the end of SETTEMBRE gives RE, the start of ESTATE gives ES, and none of those is the only one. Say so.

knobs.knob: which of the four moves is allowed
knobs.effect: All four gives a wide field and a lot of easy answers. One at a time — only middles, say — turns the same exercise into a search, and shows which of the four is hardest, which is the middle.

knobs.knob: whether a grid is around it
knobs.effect: Without a grid the clue is the whole exercise and takes one sheet and no dictionary. With a grid, filling it needs a word list and cannot be done by hand, and the small piece worth doing is buried.
Given the clue, the person works out two letters and there is one answer. Given the two letters, the person writes a clue and there are many, and the many are why this side is the one to ask.
Two letters is where this way of clueing lives and where Italian grids use it. Three or more and the trick stops working, because a longer stretch of a word is usually just the word.

where_the_work_is: In looking at how a word is written rather than at what it means, which is the move and the only one. Once seen, four clues take five minutes; before it is seen, none of the three examples make sense.
breaks: It prints as text with nothing to align, and a scanned page of handwritten clues reads. It is the one thing in its section that fits 800x480, since a clue and its two letters make one short line. Composing is entirely a matter of looking inside words — all four moves do — so every clue printed has to be checked against the word it names, one at a time.
